subject: prog-cont
title: PROG.CONT.-----TR.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-40 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan) accompanying Braxton's claim about world creativity: 'the real dynamics of world transformation will be directly proportioned to how individuals deal with the challenge of actual reality expansion — both theoretically and actually.' PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) is crossed with TR (transformation): the question is what progressional-continuance produces when crossed with transformation — under conditions where individual transcultural artistic activity is the operative scale. CRTF-D (cross-transfer definitions) and T-C-IMP (time continuum implications) branch from the main line between subject and partner. TR is partner-center. CULT-INFO-DY (culture-information dynamics) branches from the main line to the lower-left, and EXT-F (extended functionalism) runs from it across the center; AF-DY (affinity dynamics) drops from the EXT-F line to the lower-center, and INFO-DE (information degrees) rises from it on the right. AFI (affinity insight) branches from INFO-DE and anchors the right output; BSCF (basic science, or basic scientific functionalism) hangs from the AFI line on the lower-right, and (R)PART (the reality of participation) anchors the upper-right margin via a *dashed* edge from the AFI line — a dotted line amplifies some aspect of the concept it is connected to. Structural argument: progressional-continuance crossed with transformation carries its larger side structure through culture-information-dynamics and extended-functionalism, out to information-degrees and affinity-insight. The diagram is Braxton's structural case for why individual world-musicianship matters.
